senses.gloss: m. (πωλητήρ, πωλητήριον) shop-keeper, esp. seller of bakers’ ware; shop, esp. bakery-shop.
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 4:9">Ab. Zar. IV, 9</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 55b:2">55ᵇ</cite>) <he>מוליכין עמו פת לפ׳</he> you may carry your own bread with his (the non-observant baker’s) to the shop-keeper.

<cite ref="Mishnah Demai 5:4">Dem. V, 4</cite> <he>הלוקח מן הפ׳ וכ׳</he> he who buys bread at the shop (which contains bread of different batches) must give tithes of each form separately, contrad. to <cite ref="M01807"><he>מנפול</he></cite>. Y. Shek. VII, beg. 51ᵃ, a. e. <he>לוקח מן הפ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="O00584"><he>סִידְקִי</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Sheviit 7:1:16">Y. Shebi. VII, 37ᶜ</cite> top <he>ובלבד שלא יעשה פליטר</he> (not <he>יעשו</he>; R. S. to ib. VII, 3 <cite ref="Q01026"><he>פלטר</he></cite>) provided he is not made (their regular) shop-keeper (selling at the same place, at all times).
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:6">Cant. R. to I, 6</cite> <he>שנמכרת חוץ לפ׳</he> (not <he>לפלטיא</he>), v. <cite ref="S00864"><he>קַיבָר</he></cite>; a. fr.
